skill_name: task (family: task_create, task_check, task_explain, task_select, task_implement, task_audit, task_finish, task_fix)

evals.prompt: Make a task for adding request rate limiting to the public API: requests over 100 per minute should receive an HTTP 429.
evals.expected_output: Exactly one well-formed, lint-clean task file appears under tasks/ with status open and reported-by populated. created and updated are stamped from the real wall clock (a single date run), not fabricated. The description fits the ~180-char budget and the acceptance list carries task-specific checks only. No second task and no broader backlog session is run.
expectations: Exactly one new *.md task file exists under tasks/ (none under archive/).
The new file lints clean (lint.py exits 0, no blocking findings).
status is open.
reported-by is populated from the user-name chain.
created equals updated (both stamped once from one date run).
created sits within minutes of the real wall clock captured at run time — not a fabricated time-of-day (grade.sh compares it against the run-start wall clock).
The agent ran `date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S` (or otherwise produced a wall-clock value) rather than inventing a timestamp.
The frontmatter description is composed to the ~180-character budget (mechanically: at most 200 characters, under the lint warn).
'## Acceptance' is an enumerated list of task-specific checks; no generic project gate (make lint, a deploy dry-run, the full test suite) appears as an item.
No second task was created and no list/query/update workflow was run.

evals.prompt: Is the task tasks/api_make-it-better.md ready to hand to an implementer? Check it.
evals.expected_output: A readiness verdict: a '# General assessment' paragraph followed by a '## Issues' list that is NOT 'No issues found.' (the fixture task is vague with empty Approach and Acceptance). The task file is changed only to stamp status checked and bump updated.
expectations: The response leads with a '# General assessment' heading and one short readiness paragraph.
The response has a '## Issues' section.
Because the task is under-specified, the Issues section is NOT 'No issues found.' — it lists concrete problems (empty Approach/Acceptance, vague goal), ranked most-problematic-first.

Each issue follows the '**[short title]** — where it sits, what is wrong, the implementation impact, and the minimum fix' shape, locating the issue by label or unambiguous description (heading, tag, quoted phrase) per the soft-pointer rule.
Issues are grounded against the repo (the checked file was actually read); an unverifiable suspicion appears only as a question in the general assessment, never as a numbered issue.
Style-level findings, if any, sit in an unnumbered 'Style notes' tail after the list — the numbered list carries implementation-divergence risks exclusively.
The task file is changed only to stamp status: checked and bump updated.
